title: GSM A RR: de_rr_meas_res(): show padding and fix return value
description:
According to 3GPP TS 44.018 section 10.5.2.20, the `Measurement Results` is a type 3 (TV) information element with 17 (1 + 16) octets length.

The respective dissection function is called as follows:

```
  ELEM_MAND_V(GSM_A_PDU_TYPE_RR, DE_RR_MEAS_RES, ...)
    elem_v(tvb, tree, pinfo, GSM_A_PDU_TYPE_RR, DE_RR_MEAS_RES, ...)
      de_rr_meas_res(tvb, subtree, pinfo, curr_offset, -1, ...)
                                                      ^^^
                                                      len
```

Note that `elem_v()` passes -1 as the `len` argument to `de_rr_meas_res()`. The later returns -1 casted to `guint`, and this is indeed wrong. Moreover, the `len` argument is marked as unused (`_U_`). This bug creates a false impression that the `Measurement Results` IE occupies more octets than it actually does when it's encapsulated into some other protocol, e.g. A-bis/RSL.

notes.body:
Because I don't want to see:

```
Padding Bits: 0000000000000000000000000000000000000...
```

Using `proto_tree_add_bytes_format_value()` allows to "hide" the actual padding sequence:

```
Padding Bits: padding with zeroes
```

This is also how the existing code in this file references the `hf_gsm_a_rr_padding`.
So the dissection code assumes that the padding is filled with zeroes while it might not be the case, which sound like a small lie ;)

Well, I took "padding with zeroes" from 3GPP TS 44.018. We may want to actually check if padding is zeroes and print an expert warning if not. This is what e.g. `gsm_rr_csn_padding_bits()` does. Just an idea.

With `proto_tree_add_item()` I am getting this:

```
Padding Bits: f00000000000000000
```

This is also not true, 'f' is not part of the actual padding. The problem is that padding may start at an arbitrary bit offset, not necessarily at an octet boundary. This is what we see above.

With `proto_tree_add_item()` and `FT_BYTES` changed to `FT_NONE` I am getting this:

```
Padding Bits
```

I am generally fine with the second result (with `FT_NONE`). But if you guys like the idea of checking if padding bits are actually zeroes, I wold be happy to implement this. Thanks for all your suggestions!
There is (not) yet BASE_PADDING (or other stuff) for check if padding is zero (you can add on hf description)

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/8568/diffs?diff_id=520441204&start_sha=0acc8454787e46bdcab40291860f5b1cd9abbe9e#73ad6aac13b745ae2e96dfc007f503a6994c5766_4343_4346)

As a quick (and beautiful, IMO) solution I decided to generalize and use the existing `gsm_rr_csn_padding_bits()` function for checking the padding pattern. It prints "Unknown extension detected or malformed PDU (Not decoded)" if the given buffer contains something unexpected. Resolving this thread.

GSM A RR: make gsm_rr[_csn]_padding_bits() accept padding pattern

This way we can also use this function for checking padding in
the Measurement Results IE, which uses 0x00 as padding pattern.

Drop the '_csn' part because it's not CSN.1 specific anymore.
